hints: Find the y-coordinate at x = 1: y = \sqrt{2(1)^3 + 10} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}.
Differentiate y = (2x^3+10)^{1/2} with respect to x to find the tangent gradient dy/dx at x = 1.
Determine the normal gradient m_{\text{norm}} = -1/m_{\text{tan}} and write the normal equation in the form ax + by\sqrt{3} + c = 0.
walkthrough:
Find the point on the curve at $x = 1$:
$$y = \sqrt{2(1)^3 + 10} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3} \implies (1, 2\sqrt{3})$$

Evaluate the tangent gradient and normal gradient at $x = 1$:
$$m_{\text{tan}} = \frac{3(1)^2}{\sqrt{12}} = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies m_{\text{norm}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{tan}}} = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Form the equation of the normal line and rearrange:
$$y - 2\sqrt{3} = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}(x - 1) \implies \sqrt{3}(y - 2\sqrt{3}) = -2(x - 1)$$
$$\sqrt{3}y - 6 = -2x + 2 \implies 2x + \sqrt{3}y - 8 = 0$$

hints: The volume of revolution about the x-axis is given by V = \pi \int_1^3 y^2\,dx.
Integrate polynomial 2x^3 + 10 from x = 1 to x = 3 and multiply by \pi.
walkthrough:
Set up the integral for the volume of revolution about the $x$-axis:
$$V = \pi \int_1^3 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_1^3 (2x^3 + 10)\,dx$$

Subtract to find the exact volume:
$$V = \pi(70.5 - 10.5) = 60\pi$$
